mcq.q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
x: Co-designed the TCP/IP protocols that the Internet runs on, not the World Wide Web layer built on top of them.
Co-created the Mosaic browser and Netscape, which popularized the web, but he did not invent it.
Created the JavaScript language at Netscape in 1995, which is a scripting language and not the Web itself.
mcq.e: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web at CERN around 1989 to 1991, creating HTML, HTTP, and the first browser and server.

mcq.q: Which organization, founded by Tim Berners-Lee in 1994, develops web standards?
x: Develops the Internet protocols such as TCP and IP through open working groups, not the web standards.
Manages domain name system policy and IP address allocation, not HTML or CSS standards.
A professional engineering body that publishes standards such as Wi-Fi 802.11, not W3C web standards.
mcq.e: W3C, the World Wide Web Consortium, was founded by Tim Berners-Lee in 1994 and publishes the official standards for HTML, CSS, and related web technologies.

mcq.q: HTML stands for:
x: An invented expansion. The H in HTML stands for HyperText, not HighText, and Machine Language is not part of the name.
A wrong expansion. The real term is HyperText, not hyperlinks plus text.
A wrong expansion. Home Tool is not part of the name, and the H stands for HyperText.
mcq.e: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard language for structuring content on web pages using elements and tags.

mcq.q: Which tag defines the largest heading in HTML?
x: The smallest heading level in HTML, not the largest.
A container for page metadata such as the title and linked resources, not a visible heading.
A semantic element for introductory content or a group of navigation, not a heading level.
mcq.e: The h1 tag defines the top-level and largest heading, and h2 through h6 are used for progressively smaller subheadings.

mcq.q: Which HTML tag creates a hyperlink?
x: Used in the head to load external resources such as stylesheets, not to create clickable links in the body.
An attribute, not a tag. It holds the destination inside an a tag but does not create the link itself.
Not an HTML element. URLs appear as values of the href or src attributes instead.
mcq.e: The a (anchor) element creates a hyperlink, and its href attribute supplies the destination address.

mcq.q: Which attribute of provides alternative text?
x: Gives a hover tooltip on an element, not the text that screen readers read when an image cannot display.
Specifies the location of the image file, not a text description of it.
Identifies a form control for submission or scripting, and does not describe the image.
mcq.e: The alt attribute gives a text description of the image, which is shown if the image fails to load and read aloud by screen readers.

mcq.q: Which of these is a void (empty) element in HTML?
x: A paragraph container that needs an opening and closing tag and wraps text.
A generic block container that needs an opening and closing tag to hold content.
An inline container for styling part of a text, which also needs a closing tag.
mcq.e: The br element is a void element that inserts a line break and has no closing tag or content.

mcq.q: Which element should hold the main navigation links semantically?
x: Meant for lists of commands or interactive controls, not the semantic element for a site's main navigation.
Holds content tangentially related to the main content, such as a sidebar, not primary navigation.
Groups thematic content with a heading, and does not specifically mark up navigation links.
mcq.e: The nav element marks up a section of major navigation links, which helps screen readers and search engines identify site navigation.

mcq.q: Which of these is a semantic HTML5 element?
x: A generic non-semantic container that says nothing about the content it holds.
A generic inline container with no semantic meaning for the content it holds.
An inline tag for bold styling with no structural meaning for the page.
mcq.e: The article element marks up a self-contained piece of content, such as a blog post or news story, that could stand on its own.

mcq.q: Which HTML tag creates an ordered list?
x: Creates an unordered bulleted list, not a numbered one.
Marks a single list item and must sit inside ul or ol, so it does not create the list itself.
Creates a description list of term and description pairs, not a numbered list.
mcq.e: The ol element is the ordered list, and its items are numbered by default.

mcq.q: Which tag creates an unordered (bulleted) list?
x: Creates an ordered list that is numbered, not bulleted.
Marks a single list item and must sit inside ul or ol, so it does not create the list itself.
Not a valid HTML element. Bulleted lists use the ul tag.
mcq.e: The ul element is the unordered list, and its items display with bullets by default.

mcq.q: Which tag defines a table row?
x: Defines an individual data cell inside a row, not the row itself.
Defines an individual header cell inside a row, not the row itself.
Not a valid HTML element. Table rows use the tr tag.
mcq.e: The tr element defines a table row, and its td or th cells sit inside it.

mcq.q: Which HTTP method sends form data in the URL and is bookmarkable?
x: Sends data in the request body, so the form data is not visible in the URL to bookmark.
Updates or replaces a resource on the server, not used to retrieve a page with URL parameters.
Requests removal of a resource on the server, not a form-submission method for retrieving data.
mcq.e: GET sends form data as URL query parameters, which keeps the address bookmarkable and shareable, and it is meant for retrieving data.

mcq.q: Which form method sends data in the request body?
x: Places form data in the URL rather than the request body.
Works like GET but returns only headers without a body, so it does not send form data in the body.
Echoes the received request for diagnostics, not a form submission method.
mcq.e: POST sends form data in the request body, which keeps it out of the URL and suits submitting data that changes server state.

mcq.q: Which input type hides the characters being typed?
x: Stores a value in the form that users cannot see or edit, and does not mask typed characters.
Not a valid input type in HTML.
A plain visible single-line text box that shows characters as they are typed.
mcq.e: The password input type masks typed characters with dots or asterisks so that people nearby cannot read them.

mcq.q: Which input type provides a color picker?
x: Not a valid HTML input type.
A slider for choosing a number within a range, not a color.
Not a valid input type. The color picker is the input type color.
mcq.e: The color input type opens a color picker and sets a value in hex format such as #RRGGBB.

mcq.q: CSS stands for:
x: An invented expansion. The C stands for Cascading, which describes how conflicting styles are prioritized.
An invented expansion. Cascading is the correct word.
An invented expansion. CSS controls layout and appearance broadly, not only color.
mcq.e: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets, the language that controls how HTML elements look and are laid out.

mcq.q: Which is the best practice for adding CSS to many pages?
x: Applied to a single element's style attribute, so the same styles must be repeated on every element and page.
An internal style block works for one page only and must be copied to every other page.
JavaScript can change styles, but it is not a styling method and is not the standard way to style pages.
mcq.e: An external stylesheet is a separate css file linked from every page, so one change updates the whole site and browsers can cache it.

mcq.q: Which CSS selector selects elements by class?
x: A selector that targets an element by id, not by class.
A tag selector that matches elements by tag name, not by class.
Not a valid CSS selector. An asterisk selects all elements and cannot be combined this way.
mcq.e: The dot prefix selects elements that have the class attribute with that name, and one class can be shared across many elements.

mcq.q: Which CSS selector selects an element by id?
x: A class selector, which can match many elements instead of one id.
A tag selector that matches elements by tag name, not by id.
Not a valid CSS selector. The at sign starts at-rules such as media queries.
mcq.e: The hash prefix selects the element whose id attribute matches, and each id should be unique on a page.

mcq.q: Which CSS property controls text color?
x: Not a valid CSS property.
Not a valid CSS property.
Not a valid CSS property. CSS uses the color property for text.
mcq.e: The color property sets the text color of an element, and it accepts values such as named colors, hex codes, or rgb.

mcq.q: Which CSS feature applies styles based on screen width?
x: Styles parts of an element such as the before and after generated content, not styles based on screen width.
Defines the steps of a CSS animation, not rules based on screen width.
Stores reusable values using custom properties, and does not apply styles based on screen size.
mcq.e: Media queries use the at-media rule to apply CSS only when conditions such as screen width are met, which enables responsive layouts.

mcq.q: What is the HEX code for white?
x: Black, with no red, green, or blue light.
Pure red, with only the red channel at maximum.
Pure green, with only the green channel at maximum.
mcq.e: #FFFFFF sets red, green, and blue all to their maximum values, which produces white.

mcq.q: What is the HEX code for black?
x: White, with all three channels at full value.
Pure red, with only the red channel at maximum.
Pure blue, with only the blue channel at maximum.
mcq.e: #000000 sets red, green, and blue all to zero, which produces black.

mcq.q: Who created JavaScript?
x: Created Java at Sun Microsystems, which is a different language.
Invented the World Wide Web and HTML, not JavaScript.
Created PHP, a server-side language, not JavaScript.
mcq.e: Brendan Eich created JavaScript at Netscape in 1995, and it became the main scripting language of web browsers.

mcq.q: DOM stands for:
x: An incorrect expansion. The D stands for Document.
An incorrect expansion. Object Model is the correct term.
An incorrect expansion and not a web standard term.
mcq.e: DOM stands for Document Object Model, a tree-like representation of an HTML page that JavaScript can read and change.

mcq.q: Which runtime lets JavaScript run on the server using the V8 engine?
x: Deno is also a JavaScript runtime built on V8, but the answer here is Node.js, so the word only is not accurate.
The Java Virtual Machine runs Java and other JVM languages, not JavaScript on V8.
Microsoft's framework for languages such as C#, not JavaScript on V8.
mcq.e: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser on the server, built on Google's V8 engine, and is widely used for web backends.

mcq.q: UI design focuses on:
x: Describes UX design, which covers the whole customer journey and is broader than the interface look, so only is wrong.
A backend engineering concern, not UI design.
A data architecture concern, not UI design.
mcq.e: UI design focuses on the look and the interface elements users interact with, such as layout, typography, color, buttons, and icons.

mcq.q: Which design tool is browser-based and widely used for UI collaboration?
x: A plain text editor, not a design tool.
A spreadsheet program, not used for UI design.
A database design and administration tool, not a visual design tool.
mcq.e: Figma is a browser-based design tool that lets teams collaborate on interfaces in real time.

mcq.q: WCAG stands for:
x: A wrong expansion. Guidelines is the correct word.
A wrong expansion. The W3C publishes Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.
A wrong expansion. WCAG covers web content and not only coding.
mcq.e: WCAG stands for Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, published by the W3C to make web content usable by people with disabilities.

mcq.q: SEO stands for:
x: An invented expansion. SEO focuses on optimizing a site for search engines.
An invented expansion and not an industry term.
An invented expansion. Secure is not part of the term.
mcq.e: SEO stands for Search Engine Optimization, the practice of improving a site's visibility in organic search results.

mcq.q: E-commerce is best defined as:
mcq.a: Buying and selling goods and services over electronic networks
w: Running a physical store with computers
x: A narrow example of social commerce, not the full definition.
A logistics method for delivery, not what e-commerce is.
Uses technology inside a physical store, not buying and selling over electronic networks.
mcq.e: E-commerce means buying and selling goods and services over electronic networks such as the internet, without requiring a physical storefront.

mcq.q: M-commerce refers to commerce conducted through:
x: Large central computers, not the mobile devices that m-commerce uses.
A bulk email method, not a commerce channel that uses mobile devices.
A virtual world, which is narrower and does not define m-commerce.
mcq.e: M-commerce is commerce conducted through mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets, using mobile apps or mobile web browsers.

mcq.q: Who founded Amazon?
x: Co-founded Alibaba, not Amazon.
Founded eBay, not Amazon.
Known for Tesla and SpaceX, not Amazon.
mcq.e: Jeff Bezos founded Amazon in 1994 as an online bookstore that later expanded into a global marketplace.

mcq.q: Which are major Philippine e-wallets?
x: Global e-wallets from the US, not major Philippine e-wallets.
Chinese and Indian e-wallets, not Philippine ones.
US-based payment apps, not Philippine e-wallets.
mcq.e: GCash and Maya are the leading e-wallets in the Philippines, letting users pay bills, send money, and shop from mobile phones.

mcq.q: Which web browser engine is used by Chrome and Edge?
x: The engine used by Apple Safari, which is the ancestor of Blink but is not the engine in Chrome and Edge today.
The rendering engine developed by Mozilla for Firefox, not the one used by Chrome or Edge.
The legacy engine of Internet Explorer, which Edge replaced with a new engine.
mcq.e: Blink is the rendering engine forked from WebKit in 2013 and is used by Chromium-based browsers such as Chrome and Edge.

mcq.q: Which browser engine does Firefox use?
x: The engine used by Chrome and Edge, forked from WebKit, not the engine that Firefox uses.
The engine used by Apple Safari, not the one in Firefox.
The open-source project behind Chrome, which uses Blink as its engine, not Firefox's Gecko.
mcq.e: Gecko is the layout and rendering engine developed by Mozilla and used in Firefox to parse HTML and CSS and draw pages.

mcq.q: In the CSS box model, the order from inside to outside is:
x: Margin sits outside the border, and padding sits between the content and the border, so the order of padding and margin is wrong.
Reverses the whole order by starting from the outside, which is the opposite of how the box model is built.
Places padding outside the content, but padding sits between the content and the border.
mcq.e: The box model order from inside out is content, then padding, then border, then margin, which is the space outside the element.

mcq.q: Which has the highest CSS specificity?
x: Strong, but lower in specificity than inline styles.
Has lower specificity than an ID selector and inline styles.
Has the lowest specificity of these options, because it targets tags only.
mcq.e: Inline styles placed directly in the style attribute have the highest specificity, so they override ID, class, and element rules unless important is used.

mcq.q: Which CSS display value makes a one-dimensional flexible layout?
x: Creates a two-dimensional layout of rows and columns, not a one-dimensional one.
Stacks elements vertically, one per line, and does not distribute items flexibly.
Lays out content in a table structure, which is not a flexible one-dimensional model.
mcq.e: display flex creates a one-dimensional flexible layout that arranges items along a row or column and distributes space among them.

mcq.q: Which CSS framework is utility-first?
x: A component-based framework with predefined classes such as btn, not utility-first.
A framework of modular component classes built on Flexbox, not utility-first.
A framework that implements Google Material Design components, not a utility-first approach.
mcq.e: Tailwind CSS is utility-first, providing small single-purpose classes such as flex and p-4 that are combined directly in HTML.

mcq.q: Which JavaScript library created by Meta uses a virtual DOM and JSX?
x: A full framework from Google that uses TypeScript and templates rather than JSX.
A progressive framework created by Evan You, not from Meta.
A DOM manipulation library that does not use a virtual DOM or JSX.
mcq.e: React was created by Meta, using a virtual DOM to update the page efficiently and JSX syntax to write UI components.

mcq.q: Which color model is additive and used for screens?
x: A subtractive model used for printing, not for screens.
A proprietary color matching system for inks, not a color model for displays.
A traditional painting color model, not one used for screens.
mcq.e: RGB is additive, mixing red, green, and blue light to produce colors, which is how screens display color.

mcq.q: Which color model is subtractive and used for printing?
x: An additive light model used for screens, not subtractive printing.
A way to describe colors by hue, saturation, and lightness, not a print ink model.
A notation for RGB values written in hexadecimal, used in web code, not a print model.
mcq.e: CMYK is subtractive, using cyan, magenta, yellow, and black inks that absorb light, and it is the standard for color printing.

mcq.q: Colors opposite each other on the color wheel are:
x: Colors next to each other on the wheel, not opposite.
Three colors evenly spaced around the wheel, not two opposite colors.
Variations of one single hue, not opposite colors.
mcq.e: Complementary colors sit opposite each other on the color wheel, creating strong contrast when placed side by side.

mcq.q: LCP in Core Web Vitals measures:
x: Measures interactivity, which belongs to INP, not LCP.
Measures layout stability, which belongs to CLS, not LCP.
Relates to server response time, such as TTFB, while LCP measures when the main content renders.
mcq.e: LCP, Largest Contentful Paint, measures how long the largest visible element takes to render, which reflects loading performance.

mcq.q: Which file tells search engine crawlers which pages not to crawl?
x: Lists pages the site wants indexed, the opposite of telling crawlers what to avoid.
An Apache server configuration file for settings such as redirects, not a crawler instruction file.
A common homepage file, not a crawler instruction file.
mcq.e: robots.txt sits at the site root and uses Disallow rules to tell crawlers which paths they should not crawl.

mcq.q: Amazon, Lazada and Shopee are examples of:
x: Business to business, where both parties are companies. These platforms sell to individual consumers.
Consumer to consumer, where individuals sell to each other, such as on eBay or Carousell.
Business to government, such as selling to public agencies.
mcq.e: Amazon, Lazada, and Shopee sell goods from businesses to individual consumers, which is business to consumer, or B2C.

mcq.q: eBay and Carousell are examples of:
x: Businesses sell to consumers, but eBay and Carousell are mainly individual sellers.
Business to business, where companies trade with each other.
Government to citizen, such as public services delivered to residents.
mcq.e: eBay and Carousell let individual consumers sell to other individual consumers, so they are consumer to consumer, or C2C.

mcq.q: Selling products without holding inventory, with the supplier shipping directly, is:
x: The seller buys goods in bulk and holds inventory, which dropshipping avoids.
The seller holds goods owned by another party and pays only when items sell, so it involves holding stock.
A model where a franchisor licenses its brand and system to franchisees, not a supplier-shipping model.
mcq.e: Dropshipping lets sellers list products without holding inventory, so the supplier ships each order directly to the customer.

mcq.q: The security standard for organizations that handle card data is:
x: A US law on health information privacy, not card data security.
A quality management standard, not card data security.
The Sarbanes-Oxley Act on financial reporting controls for public companies, not card data.
mcq.e: PCI DSS is the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard, which sets security requirements for organizations that store, process, or transmit card data.

mcq.q: Conversion rate is computed as:
x: Visitors divided by orders is the inverse ratio, giving how many visitors each order needs, not the share of visitors who buy.
Revenue divided by visitors is revenue per visitor, a different metric that measures money earned rather than the share of visitors who convert.
Clicks divided by impressions is the click-through rate, which measures ad response, not purchase conversion.
mcq.e: Conversion rate is the share of visitors who place an order, so orders divided by visitors gives it. It fits because the question asks how visitors turn into buyers.

mcq.q: CTR is computed as:
x: Impressions divided by clicks is the inverse of CTR and gives a number that is not a click rate.
Orders divided by clicks is a click-to-order conversion measure, not click-through rate.
Clicks divided by orders gives clicks per order, not the share of impressions that receive a click.
mcq.e: CTR is click-through rate, the share of impressions that receive a click. It fits because it compares clicks to impressions to measure how appealing an ad is.

mcq.q: Which BSP-standard QR code allows interoperable payments in the Philippines?
x: A generic phrase, not the BSP standard name.
An invented name, not the BSP standard.
An invented name. The BSP is the regulator, not the name of the QR standard.
mcq.e: QR Ph is the BSP-standard QR code that lets payment apps from different providers work together across the Philippines.

mcq.q: In a card payment, which party is the customer's own bank that approves or declines the transaction?
mcq.e: The issuer issued the card and holds the customer's account. The acquirer serves the merchant, and the card network (Visa/Mastercard) routes the messages between them.
x: The acquirer is the merchant's bank that processes card payments for the seller, not the bank that approves the customer's card.
The payment gateway passes transaction data between the merchant and the processors; it does not hold the customer's account.
The card network, such as Visa or Mastercard, routes transaction messages between banks and sets rules; it does not hold the customer's account.

mcq.q: Which Philippine law is the Data Privacy Act?
x: RA 10175 is the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, which covers online offenses, not personal data protection.
RA 8792 is the Electronic Commerce Act of 2000, which covers electronic transactions, not personal data privacy.
RA 7394 is the Consumer Act of the Philippines, which protects consumers in trade, not personal data privacy.
mcq.e: RA 10173 is the Data Privacy Act of 2012, which protects personal information and created the National Privacy Commission. It fits because the question asks for the data privacy law.

mcq.q: A request returns HTTP 403. What does this mean?
mcq.a: The server understood the request but refuses to authorize it
w: The requested resource was not found
The client must authenticate because credentials are missing or invalid
The server crashed while handling the request
mcq.e: 403 Forbidden means access is refused even if you are known. 401 is the one for missing or invalid credentials, 404 is Not Found, and 500 is an internal server error.
x: 404 Not Found means the resource does not exist, not that access is refused.
401 Unauthorized means credentials are missing or invalid, not that the server understood the request and refused it.
500 Internal Server Error means the server failed while processing the request, not an authorization refusal.

mcq.q: HTTP stands for:
mcq.e: HTTP is the protocol browsers and servers use to exchange web pages.
x: No such protocol name exists.
No such protocol name exists.
No such protocol name exists.

mcq.q: Which HTML element contains the visible content of a web page?
mcq.e: The body element holds everything displayed in the browser window.
x: The head holds metadata, not visible content.
The title only sets the tab title.
The meta element only describes the document.

mcq.q: URL stands for:
mcq.e: A URL is the address that locates a resource on the web.
x: Not the standard expansion.
Not the standard expansion.
Not the standard expansion.

mcq.q: Which attribute of the tag specifies the image file to display?
mcq.e: The src attribute gives the path or URL of the image.
x: href is used on links, not images.
alt gives alternative text only.
link is not an img attribute.

mcq.q: Which HTTP status code means Not Found?
mcq.e: 404 tells the client the requested resource does not exist.
x: 200 means OK.
301 means moved permanently.
500 means internal server error.

mcq.q: Which JavaScript method selects an element by its id?
mcq.e: getElementById returns the element whose id matches.
x: No such DOM method exists.
No such DOM method exists.
No such DOM method exists.

mcq.q: Which rendering engine does Apple's Safari browser use?
mcq.e: Safari is built on WebKit.
x: Blink powers Chrome and Edge.
Gecko powers Firefox.
Trident was used by old Internet Explorer.
